assumptions: The Airflow retry policy (2 retries, 5 minutes apart) is DAG-level configuration outside the four components and is not modelled in them.
The run date is the scheduled date {ds}, and the day folder is named exactly {ds} (YYYY-MM-DD).
"Overwrite existing files" maps to delivery.if_exists = overwrite.
Local source and destination paths are set per environment, so they are <REQUIRED>.
The package name is {source}_{ds_nodash}. It is not used in the delivered paths.

destination.name: lab_lake
destination.requirement: Deliver to the local lake folder. Each package file goes to <run date>/ under the lake folder (run date = {ds}, YYYY-MM-DD), keeping the package paths, e.g. <lake>/2024-03-01/SITE_0001/a.csv. Files are copied unchanged, never moved: the source folder is left untouched. Files that already exist in the lake are overwritten. After all files are delivered, an empty _SUCCESS marker file is written in <lake>/<run date>/, and only then (never if any file failed).

source.name: lab_drop
source.requirement: Read from the local drop folder. Only the subfolder named after the run date (YYYY-MM-DD, i.e. {ds}) is read; other day folders are ignored. Everything under that day's folder forms exactly one package per run. Take every file whose name ends in ".csv" (lowercase extension, case-sensitive; so UPPER.CSV is not taken), at any depth under the day's folder, including directly in it. All other files are ignored silently. Paths in the package are relative to the day's folder, e.g. SITE_0001/a.csv. The run fails when the day's folder contains no .csv file at all. The drop folder is never modified.

output.summary: A daily schedule (@daily) starts one run with no events. The source lists the local drop folder's subfolder named after the run date and keeps only files ending in lowercase ".csv" at any depth. It fails the run if there are none. All of them form one package, with paths relative to the day's folder. Files are delivered unchanged, with no transformation. The destination copies the package into the local lake folder under <run date>/, overwrites existing files, and writes an empty _SUCCESS marker after all files are delivered. The drop folder is never changed. Airflow retries a failed run twice, 5 minutes apart.
